title: The Transformation of Modern Football Through Match Analysis and Data Analysis
author: Matteo Juraga
description: In modern football, the integration of match analysis and data analysis has led to a radical transformation, even questioning, if not upsetting, the usual evaluation parameters. The use of these technologies allows clubs to assess more precisely some crucial aspects, in particular player performance, the optimization of tactics and game strategies, and even injury prevention. The objective is to identify and then provide more solid and precise criteria so that market decisions can be made even more informed and strategic, minimizing risks and enhancing overall performance.
The Rise of Match Analysis

Match analysis involves the detailed examination of matches through the collection and processing of quantitative data. This practice, enabled by technological advances, makes it possible to precisely analyze both individual player performance and team movements. Introduced in Italy by pioneering figures like Adriano Bacconi during the 2006 World Cup, this approach has since become a staple in the country’s football landscape.

A particularly interesting aspect of this revolution is the use of Expected Goals (xG), an index that measures the likelihood of a shot resulting in a goal based on factors like shooting position and defensive pressure. For instance, data analysis from the 2019/2020 Premier League season showed how Liverpool outperformed Manchester City in converting chances into goals. Such insights help teams better understand their efficiency and refine their strategies

Additionally, the Heat Map of Rodrigo Hernández (Rodri) illustrates the areas of the field he covered most during the previous season. This visual representation aids in understanding the player’s tactical and strategic behavior, along with his areas of influence during matches—information that was nearly impossible to obtain with precision just a few years ago.
Innovation and Advanced Metrics

Liverpool FC represents one of the best examples of how a data-driven approach can make a difference. Under the leadership of Ian Graham, Liverpool has adopted a scientific approach to match management and player selection. One of the most innovative metrics developed by Graham’s team is Goal Probability Added (GPA), which allows them to measure the impact of each player’s individual action on the overall probability of scoring a goal. This methodology has helped the club identify talents like Mohamed Salah, optimize strategic decisions, and maximize team performance.

Another standout metric is PPDA (Passes Per Defensive Action), which measures a team’s pressing intensity by calculating how many passes an opposing team can make before the defense executes a decisive action.
Machine Learning and Injury Prevention

The use of machine learning has also revolutionized injury prevention. By processing large volumes of sports data, clubs can prevent injuries before they occur by monitoring parameters such as workload, heart rate, and recovery speed. For example, Liverpool is one of the clubs that uses advanced algorithms to monitor this data and create predictive models capable of identifying risk factors, such as an overload of training that could lead to serious injuries and prolonged recovery periods. This approach enables teams to better protect and preserve their players, minimizing competitive setbacks.
Data Analysis and Market Strategy

Data analysis has also transformed scouting strategies and contract negotiations. Clubs such as Brentford and Liverpool are using data analysis to uncover hidden talents and evaluate how well a player might fit their style of play. Through this approach, Liverpool has been able to acquire key players such as Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker, solving specific tactical problems and improving the team’s overall performance. A notable example of how data analysis is influencing contract negotiations is the case of Kevin De Bruyne, who, in 2021, chose to negotiate his contract with Manchester City without enlisting the help of a proxy, but instead relying on detailed analysis of his performance to prove his worth to the club. With the help of a team of data analysis experts, De Bruyne was able to secure a highly favorable contract, showcasing how data can become an empowering tool even for the players themselves.

In conclusion, this analysis highlights how the integration of match analysis and data analysis is profoundly transforming the world of modern soccer, affecting both performance on the pitch and the economic and strategic management of clubs. The adoption of these technologies allows for more accurate and functional decision-making as well as better resource management, as is well demonstrated by the sustainable success of teams like Liverpool. However, it is important to remember that the human element remains fundamental and necessary: the intuition, experience, and sensitivity of coaches and sports managers are still essential to interpret and apply data in the real-world context. Although Artificial Intelligence can now offer undeniable supports, players' psychological and character variables continue to play a crucial role, and managing them requires an approach that goes beyond numbers. Because the unpredictability of the emotions of the moment can be decisive. For better or for worse. And that is precisely the beauty not only of soccer, but of life.

title: The Power of Classical Drama in Advertising: How Stories Shape Consumer Reactions
author: Eleftheria Topaloglou
description: In today’s fast-paced digital world, ads that tell powerful stories stand out. One of the most effective storytelling frameworks is rooted in classical drama, using time-tested narrative structures to connect with viewers on a deep emotional level. This approach doesn’t just entertain; it influences how consumers feel about brands, driving purchase intent and brand loyalty.
Here’s a closer look at how classical drama narratives work in advertising and how they can shape consumer reactions.
What Makes Classical Drama Narratives So Effective?

Classical drama narratives follow a story arc known as Freytag’s Pyramid—a structure originating in ancient theater, consisting of five stages: exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and denouement. This “inverted V” approach builds tension and emotional engagement, reaching a climax before leading viewers to a satisfying resolution. It’s this journey through a fully developed story arc that holds viewer attention, sparking positive emotional responses and empathy for the characters.

These structured narratives are particularly powerful in advertising because they create a sense of narrative transportation. When viewers are transported, they experience the story on a personal level, almost as if they are part of it. This immersion makes the ad’s message feel more authentic and the brand more relatable, which can lead to a stronger connection and a more favorable perception.
Narrative Transportation: The Key to Consumer Engagement

When consumers are fully engaged, they are less likely to critique the ad’s message. Instead of analyzing the persuasive intent, they become emotionally connected, which can diminish skepticism. This makes narrative transportation a powerful tool for brands looking to create meaningful connections.

title: Streaming Platforms and Traditional TV: The Power of Sports
author: Sabrina Frigerio
description: In recent years, sports have solidified their position as an indispensable pillar for the success of both television broadcasters and streaming platforms. Its ability to capture the interest of a wide audience, from football enthusiasts to fans of less common disciplines, has intensified the competition among various industry players. This article analyzes the evolution of sports on television and streaming platforms, and why it remains an essential type of content.

The central theme of this study concerns the driving force of sports in the television and streaming landscape. Through analyses and market research, the aim is to answer key questions: Is sport truly a strong attraction for the audience? Which platforms dominate the television and streaming sectors? How and where do consumers watch sports events?

To answer these questions, it is first necessary to examine the Italian television landscape and the relevant sector. The Italian TV market is divided into three main groups: traditional TV, pay TV, and streaming platforms. Traditional TV includes broadcasters such as Rai and Mediaset, while pay TV services are offered by Sky. Innovations in the streaming field include platforms like Netflix, DAZN, etc., which are radically transforming the way sports content is consumed, offering users greater flexibility and personalized access.

Over the years, sports have found their place first in television schedules and, more recently, on streaming platforms. In the 1990s, only free-to-air TV broadcasted sports. Today, traditional TV continues to play an important role in broadcasting sports events, but dedicated sports platforms and pay TV services have emerged. Leading the way is Sky, which boasts an average of over 8,000 hours of live sports events, along with the streaming platform DAZN.

To understand viewing habits, a quantitative analysis was conducted using the CAWI (Computer Assisted Web Interviewing) technique. The sample, composed mainly of women aged 18 to 30 from Lombardy, turned out to be quite sporty. Only 14.4% declared that they were not interested in sports, while 44.8% showed a strong interest, and 40.8% stated that they only follow major events like the Olympics and World Cup. Additionally, 60% of respondents regularly participate in sports, demonstrating not only passive interest but also active involvement in sports.
